summary.oneLiner: Laurus Labs accelerated its transformation in FY26 with CDMO revenue crossing INR 2,000 crores (+38% small molecule) and EBITDA margins expanding to 26.8%, driven by commercial NCE launches and operational leverage. Management guided for aggressive capex of INR 3,000 crores over the next two years to double down on large-scale fermentation, peptides, and greenfield units, targeting a 50% CDMO revenue mix by 2030 while maintaining steady absolute ARV sales.
summary.business: Laurus Labs is an integrated pharmaceutical and biotechnology company holding a leadership position in developing and manufacturing select Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and Finished Dosage Forms (FDF) across anti-retroviral, oncology, cardiovascular and gastro therapeutics. It also offers end-to-end Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisation (CDMO/CMO) services, supporting global innovators across human health, animal health, specialty chemicals and crop science ingredients, and is expanding beyond small molecules into biotechnology, large molecules, and cell and gene therapies.

Affordable Medicines - API: Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients across anti-retroviral (ARV), oncology, cardiovascular and gastro therapeutics
Affordable Medicines - FDF: Finished dosage forms / oral solid dosage (OSD) formulations - tablets and capsules
CDMO - Small Molecules: Complex chemistry APIs and intermediates for innovator/biotech customers
CDMO - Bio: Process development for gene therapy and antibody-drug conjugates (ADC)

currentContext.strengths: Integrated one-stop platform spanning clinical-stage development to commercial manufacturing across Affordable Medicines and CDMO|Global leadership position in select APIs (ARV, oncology, cardiovascular, gastro) with backward-integration capability|Scale and regulatory reach: 15 manufacturing sites globally accredited by USFDA, WHO, EMA and others, operated under a single quality standard for all markets|R&D depth: 6 R&D sites, 3,134 scientists/quality-team strength, 244 patents granted, 94+ DS/DP launches, and technology platforms across flow chemistry, biocatalysis, fermentation and peptides|Diversified, broad-based CDMO pipeline of 125+ active projects across human health, animal health and crop science, reducing customer/program concentration|20 years of industry track record with a global customer base of 275+ clients across 61 countries
currentContext.strategies: Improve utilisation and expand the product portfolio in the API/Affordable Medicines business while strengthening participation across developed and emerging markets|Drive closer integration between APIs and formulations to support reliable supply, cost competitiveness and faster execution|FDF: deepen position in ARV formulations while building a calibrated portfolio in select molecules; progress product filings/approvals, expand oral solid dosage (OSD) capacity, and add products under CMO to improve utilisation|Execute the KRKA joint-venture formulations platform to support access to regulated markets|Small Molecules CDMO: deepen strategic customer partnerships, invest in differentiated technology platforms (biocatalysis, flow chemistry, trickle-bed processing, peptides), and expand development/manufacturing capacity|Bio CDMO: build a diversified pipeline, scale fermentation capacity, strengthen downstream processing infrastructure and enzymatic-technology capability, and deepen long-term customer partnerships|Group-wide: deepen strategic customer relationships, advance technology-led capabilities, expand commercial capacity and maintain quality/execution standards across the development-to-commercialisation cycle|Reinvestment-led: the Company continues to direct capital toward capacity and technology expansion, including the newly allotted Laurus Pharma Zone land in Anakapalli District (projected multi-phase investment over eight years) and ongoing investment programmes across small molecule, fermentation, peptides and gene therapy/ADC platforms; capex intensity is expected to increase over FY27-28 to support these growth projects. Alongside reinvestment, the Company follows a policy of returning capital to shareholders through interim dividends (1st and 2nd interim dividends declared for FY26), while the strategic narrative emphasises 'ARV de-risking' via a rising CDMO revenue share and maintaining a strong balance sheet to fund the capex programme.
currentContext.expansion: Laurus continued to expand its integrated manufacturing platform during FY26, anchored in Visakhapatnam (API, drug substance and finished-dosage facilities), complemented by fermentation capabilities in Bengaluru, development infrastructure in Hyderabad, and cell-therapy manufacturing through associate ImmunoACT in Mumbai. Capital allocation remained focused on growth-oriented API and CDMO manufacturing expansion; FY26 capex was ₹1,070 crore (16% of revenue), taking cumulative capex from FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26 to over ₹4,350 crore. Key ongoing/recently completed projects: (1) commercial-scale peptides manufacturing - several peptide synthesisers were installed and qualified during the year along with purification and isolation capabilities; (2) client-specific CMO oral dosage capacity, which became operational during the year, supported by an additional packaging line, with the full commercial production line expected to start from June 2026; (3) the Vizag microbial fermentation facility, with Phase 1 capacity of around 400 KL planned, on track for operations by end-2026; (4) a Gene Therapy/ADC cGMP facility in Hyderabad (groundbreaking June 2025) built for plasmid DNA, viral vectors (e.g. AAV), bioconjugation, lyophilisation and sterile fill-finish, with planned investment in the site of over ₹200 crore and expected completion by end-2026; (5) commercial spray-drying capability, identified as one of the capability additions within the FY26 manufacturing build-out; and (6) the KRKA JV FDF facility, with construction going as per plan and Phase-1 manufacturing blocks expected to be ready by mid-2027.
currentContext.mdna: Global pharmaceutical industry growth (9.3% in 2025) driven by chronic-disease prevalence, R&D investment, rising healthcare expenditure and broader access to medicines|Global generics market growth (est. 6.5% CAGR to USD 770.0 billion by 2033) driven by patent expiries and sustained demand for affordable medicines|Global small-molecule CDMO market expansion (USD76.1bn in 2025 toward ~USD145.5bn by 2035) driven by rising outsourcing and development complexity|Global industrial biotechnology and precision-fermentation markets expanding rapidly, supporting the Bio CDMO opportunity set|Customers rebalancing sourcing networks to reduce geographic concentration, positioning India (and Laurus) to benefit from supply-chain diversification|Near-term FDF performance may continue to reflect procurement cycles and product-mix dynamics, though underlying demand environment remains resilient|Tender cycles, pricing dynamics and approval timelines may continue to influence near-term phasing in the FDF business|Bio CDMO: discussions for longer-term manufacturing contracts progressing, improving revenue visibility into FY 2026-27 and beyond|Vendor diversification, rising chemistry complexity and customer preference for strategic end-to-end partners continue to support the small-molecule CDMO opportunity|Small Molecules CDMO: active pipeline of more than 125 projects, including over 102 in human health and around 23 in animal health and crop science|Bio CDMO: building a diversified pipeline across customers, applications and fermentation platforms, with continued pipeline progress on larger global accounts|FDF: cumulative product dossier filings reached 94, with 7 dossiers filed and 6 approvals received during FY26

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict disrupting trade, energy costs and supply chains
risks.note: The Middle East war involving the US, Israel and Iran (which began February 28, 2026) caused India's exports to West Asia to fall 57.95% in March 2026; management flags this conflict as a source of sharply higher crude oil prices, disrupted energy supply and pressure on input costs and raw-material availability going into FY27.

risks.risk: Rising trade protectionism and tariffs on exports
risks.note: FY26 brought heightened uncertainty in global trade and the imposition of high, punitive tariffs by key trading partners on India; fluctuating trade policies are cited as a continuing source of uncertainty for the operating environment.

India's GDP growth is projected to decline from an estimated 7.6% in FY26 to 6.9% in FY27, with management citing heightened uncertainty and rising economic risk tied to the Middle East conflict and its effect on energy infrastructure in Gulf nations.

The Board's Report references a Risk Management framework intended to recognise, evaluate and mitigate 'various foreseeable threats' across business segments amid an evolving external environment, but explicitly directs readers to a detailed risk discussion elsewhere in the Integrated Annual Report that is not included in this bundle.

one-line thesis: Laurus Labs accelerated its transformation in FY26 with CDMO revenue crossing INR 2,000 crores (+38% small molecule) and EBITDA margins expanding to 26.8%, driven by commercial NCE launches and operational leverage. Management guided for aggressive capex of INR 3,000 crores over the next two years to double down on large-scale fermentation, peptides, and greenfield units, targeting a 50% CDMO revenue mix by 2030 while maintaining steady absolute ARV sales.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 6,813 cr (+23% YoY); Q4: INR 1,812 cr (+5% YoY). EBITDA: INR 1,826 cr (26.8% margin, +670 bps YoY); Q4: 28.9%. PAT: INR 889 cr (+148% YoY); Q4: INR 279 cr. Order Book: Robust visibility in CDMO with 3 new commercial APIs launched in last 18 months; no specific $ value disclosed. Net Debt: INR 2,285 cr (Debt/EBITDA improved to 1.25x from 2.3x). One-offs: Margin expansion driven by product mix shift to CDMO, raw material price softening, and process improvements; no major accounting distortions noted.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Double-digit growth expected in CDMO and Generics for FY27 (no specific % given). Margin: Confident in maintaining/improving ~29% EBITDA margins in FY27. Order Inflow: Strong pipeline of late-stage programs converting to commercial; no concentration risk. Capex: INR 3,000 crores planned over next 2 years (FY27-FY28), up from prior INR 1,000 cr/year guidance; 90% towards mid/large-scale manufacturing.
order book & pipeline: CDMO pipeline robust with multiple late-stage programs; 3 APIs moved to commercial in last 18 months with multi-year patent life; management cites 'very good visibility' for fermentation projects moving from Bangalore to Vizag; no quantitative order book value provided but emphasized lack of destocking risks compared to peers.
segment / subsidiary detail: CDMO: INR 2,080 cr full year (+38% small molecule to INR 1,896 cr); Q4 small molecule INR 524 cr. Affordable Medicines: INR 4,733 cr full year (+18%); Q4 INR 1,223 cr. ARV sales ~INR 2,800 cr (flat absolute, declining % mix to 41%). Laurus Bio: Q4 sales INR 65 cr (+124% YoY); Full year +15%. Non-ARV formulations growing.
growth verticals / optionality: Unit 7 Greenfield (2,000+ cum reactor volume) by Mar '27/FY '28; Commercial Peptide block validation Q2 FY27; Laurus Bio Phase 1 fermentation operational end-2026 (400 KL); Animal Health capacity at Unit 10; KRKA JV formulation facility Phase 1 by mid-2027; Long-term target of 50% revenue from CDMO by 2030.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin: 60.4% (FY26) vs 55% (FY25); Q4 at 61.4%. Drivers: Better product mix (higher CDMO share), raw material price softening, process improvements. Cost Headwinds: Some solvent price increase impact in Q4, but manageable via mix and utilization. Operating Leverage: Expected to play out significantly in FY27 as new capacities utilize.
capex / expansion: FY26 Spend: INR 1,070 cr (INR 335 cr in Q4); >75% into CDMO/CMO capabilities. Future Guidance: INR 3,000 cr over next 2 years. Key Projects: Unit 7 (small molecule), Peptide block, Fermentation (Vizag), Animal Health, KRKA JV facility.
capital allocation: Priority on high-value business segments (CDMO, Biologics, Peptides) to drive long-term growth. Debt/EBITDA targeted to remain stable or soften despite gross debt increase for capex. ROCE improved to 17.7% from 9.7%.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical disruptions impacting raw material availability/logistics (near-term OTIF pressure); Solvent price volatility; Execution risk on large greenfield capex (Unit 7, Fermentation); Regulatory audit outcomes (though 132 audits passed without critical findings in FY26); Potential lumpiness in quarterly CDMO earnings despite annual growth.
management quality / tone: Highly confident and aggressive on capex; transparent about margin drivers; defensive on customer concentration (denies destocking risks); focused on 'strategic partnership' model over tactical; emphasizes scale and technology platforms (biocatalysis, continuous manufacturing).
non-obvious takeaways: Fermentation expansion initially targeting non-pharma/industrial chemicals (surfactants, polymers) to de-risk yield/contamination before pharma scale-up; CDMO definition strictly excludes generic CMO revenues; ARV absolute sales expected to remain flat (~INR 2,800 cr) while % mix shrinks; Peptide capex described as 'large' but specific numbers withheld.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inventory destocking concerns plaguing Indian CDMO peers; raw material inflation | Divi's Laboratories | beneficiary | Med | Laurus' confirmation of no destocking issues and strong commercial pipeline validates sector resilience, potentially re-rating peers with similar late-stage exposure. |
| Margin compression in generic ARV space; supply chain disruptions | Granules India | beneficiary | Low | Laurus' ability to maintain ARV volumes despite geopolitical headwinds suggests stable demand environment for integrated ARV players. |
| High capex intensity and execution risk in biologics/fermentation | Small-cap Biotech Firms | loser | Med | Laurus' aggressive INR 3,000 cr capex plan in fermentation and peptides raises the barrier to entry, potentially squeezing smaller players lacking scale. |

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.

Capex: INR 3,000 crores planned over next 2 years (FY27-FY28), up from prior INR 1,000 cr/year guidance; 90% towards mid/large-scale manufacturing.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Unit 7 Greenfield (2,000+ cum reactor volume) by Mar '27/FY '28; Commercial Peptide block validation Q2 FY27; Laurus Bio Phase 1 fermentation operational end-2026 (400 KL); Animal Health capacity at Unit 10; KRKA JV formulation facility Phase 1 by mid-2027; Long-term target of 50% revenue from CDMO by 2030.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global pharmaceutical industry growth (9.3% in 2025) driven by chronic-disease prevalence, R&D investment, rising healthcare expenditure and broader access to medicines
- Global generics market growth (est. 6.5% CAGR to USD 770.0 billion by 2033) driven by patent expiries and sustained demand for affordable medicines
- Global small-molecule CDMO market expansion (USD76.1bn in 2025 toward ~USD145.5bn by 2035) driven by rising outsourcing and development complexity
- Global industrial biotechnology and precision-fermentation markets expanding rapidly, supporting the Bio CDMO opportunity set
- Customers rebalancing sourcing networks to reduce geographic concentration, positioning India (and Laurus) to benefit from supply-chain diversification
- Near-term FDF performance may continue to reflect procurement cycles and product-mix dynamics, though underlying demand environment remains resilient
- Tender cycles, pricing dynamics and approval timelines may continue to influence near-term phasing in the FDF business
- Bio CDMO: discussions for longer-term manufacturing contracts progressing, improving revenue visibility into FY 2026-27 and beyond
- Vendor diversification, rising chemistry complexity and customer preference for strategic end-to-end partners continue to support the small-molecule CDMO opportunity
- Small Molecules CDMO: active pipeline of more than 125 projects, including over 102 in human health and around 23 in animal health and crop science
- Bio CDMO: building a diversified pipeline across customers, applications and fermentation platforms, with continued pipeline progress on larger global accounts
- FDF: cumulative product dossier filings reached 94, with 7 dossiers filed and 6 approvals received during FY26

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross Margin: 60.4% (FY26) vs 55% (FY25); Q4 at 61.4%. Drivers: Better product mix (higher CDMO share), raw material price softening, process improvements. Cost Headwinds: Some solvent price increase impact in Q4, but manageable via mix and utilization. Operating Leverage: Expected to play out significantly in FY27 as new capacities utilize.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority on high-value business segments (CDMO, Biologics, Peptides) to drive long-term growth. Debt/EBITDA targeted to remain stable or soften despite gross debt increase for capex. ROCE improved to 17.7% from 9.7%.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Laurus continued to expand its integrated manufacturing platform during FY26, anchored in Visakhapatnam (API, drug substance and finished-dosage facilities), complemented by fermentation capabilities in Bengaluru, development infrastructure in Hyderabad, and cell-therapy manufacturing through associate ImmunoACT in Mumbai. Capital allocation remained focused on growth-oriented API and CDMO manufacturing expansion; FY26 capex was ₹1,070 crore (16% of revenue), taking cumulative capex from FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26 to over ₹4,350 crore. Key ongoing/recently completed projects: (1) commercial-scale peptides manufacturing - several peptide synthesisers were installed and qualified during the year along with purification and isolation capabilities; (2) client-specific CMO oral dosage capacity, which became operational during the year, supported by an additional packaging line, with the full commercial production line expected to start from June 2026; (3) the Vizag microbial fermentation facility, with Phase 1 capacity of around 400 KL planned, on track for operations by end-2026; (4) a Gene Therapy/ADC cGMP facility in Hyderabad (groundbreaking June 2025) built for plasmid DNA, viral vectors (e.g. AAV), bioconjugation, lyophilisation and sterile fill-finish, with planned investment in the site of over ₹200 crore and expected completion by end-2026; (5) commercial spray-drying capability, identified as one of the capability additions within the FY26 manufacturing build-out; and (6) the KRKA JV FDF facility, with construction going as per plan and Phase-1 manufacturing blocks expected to be ready by mid-2027.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident and aggressive on capex; transparent about margin drivers; defensive on customer concentration (denies destocking risks); focused on 'strategic partnership' model over tactical; emphasizes scale and technology platforms (biocatalysis, continuous manufacturing).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated one-stop platform spanning clinical-stage development to commercial manufacturing across Affordable Medicines and CDMO
- Global leadership position in select APIs (ARV, oncology, cardiovascular, gastro) with backward-integration capability
- Scale and regulatory reach: 15 manufacturing sites globally accredited by USFDA, WHO, EMA and others, operated under a single quality standard for all markets
- R&D depth: 6 R&D sites, 3,134 scientists/quality-team strength, 244 patents granted, 94+ DS/DP launches, and technology platforms across flow chemistry, biocatalysis, fermentation and peptides
- Diversified, broad-based CDMO pipeline of 125+ active projects across human health, animal health and crop science, reducing customer/program concentration
- 20 years of industry track record with a global customer base of 275+ clients across 61 countries

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical disruptions impacting raw material availability/logistics (near-term OTIF pressure); Solvent price volatility; Execution risk on large greenfield capex (Unit 7, Fermentation); Regulatory audit outcomes (though 132 audits passed without critical findings in FY26); Potential lumpiness in quarterly CDMO earnings despite annual growth.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Fermentation expansion initially targeting non-pharma/industrial chemicals (surfactants, polymers) to de-risk yield/contamination before pharma scale-up; CDMO definition strictly excludes generic CMO revenues; ARV absolute sales expected to remain flat (~INR 2,800 cr) while % mix shrinks; Peptide capex described as 'large' but specific numbers withheld.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inventory destocking concerns plaguing Indian CDMO peers; raw material inflation | Divi's Laboratories | beneficiary | Med | Laurus' confirmation of no destocking issues and strong commercial pipeline validates sector resilience, potentially re-rating peers with similar late-stage exposure. |
| Margin compression in generic ARV space; supply chain disruptions | Granules India | beneficiary | Low | Laurus' ability to maintain ARV volumes despite geopolitical headwinds suggests stable demand environment for integrated ARV players. |
| High capex intensity and execution risk in biologics/fermentation | Small-cap Biotech Firms | loser | Med | Laurus' aggressive INR 3,000 cr capex plan in fermentation and peptides raises the barrier to entry, potentially squeezing smaller players lacking scale. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [JV] A joint venture with KRKA is building a dedicated FDF site in Hyderabad, with Phase-I high-potent and general OSD blocks slated to open in mid-2027.
- [In-licensing] Two ADC assets were in-licensed from Aarvik Therapeutics for development and commercialisation in the India market.
- [Subsidiary] ImmunoACT, the CAR-T cell therapy platform, is being showcased internationally (Bharat Innovates 2026, France) with strategic priorities of accelerating NexCar19 adoption, portfolio expansion and global partnerships/licensing.
- [Milestone] The deck is branded around the company's 20-year anniversary.
